report:
## Conclusion: The claim is well-supported

Strong evidence from randomized controlled trials, long-term follow-up, and real-world data confirms that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) significantly reduces shingles risk in adults aged 70 and older.

**Key evidence:**

1. **Pivotal RCT (ZOE-70):** In the phase III trial published in NEJM, RZV given to adults ≥70 reduced the risk of herpes zoster with vaccine efficacy exceeding 90%, and also reduced postherpetic neuralgia. This trial specifically enrolled adults 70+ and found efficacy consistent across the 70–79 and ≥80 subgroups (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800).

2. **Combined ZOE-50/ZOE-70 analysis:** Pooled data confirmed overall efficacy of 97.2% (95% CI, 93.7–99.0) against shingles, with efficacy of 96.6–97.9% consistent across all age groups, including those 70+ (https://scispace.com/papers/efficacy-of-an-adjuvanted-herpes-zoster-subunit-vaccine-in-1bjyofhdkz).

3. **Long-term durability:** Extension studies of ZOE-50/ZOE-70 show RZV confers long-term protection against herpes zoster over up to 11 years of follow-up, indicating efficacy is durable rather than transient in this older population (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353370157).

4. **Real-world/post-market confirmation:** Post-licensure effectiveness studies (e.g., in CID) corroborate the trial-derived >90% efficacy figures translate into real-world protection among vaccinated older populations (https://academic.oup.com/cid/article/73/6/941/6134290).

**Bottom line:** Multiple high-quality, peer-reviewed randomized trials (the gold standard), corroborated by extension studies and real-world observational data, consistently demonstrate that RZV substantially reduces herpes zoster incidence in adults 70 years and older, with efficacy estimates generally above 90%. This is a well-substantiated, evidence-based claim, not merely a manufacturer assertion.
